requirements.evidence: The whole contract is implemented. Migrations have cascading FKs, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16-30). Queue and Ticket models have the required casts and relations, and Entity::queues() is added (Entity.php:46). nextCode orders by id desc, skips codes that don't match /^A(\d+)$/ and pads to 3 digits (Ticket.php:95-112). IssueTicket rejects a negative priority before the transaction, locks the queue row and re-reads it ('lockForUpdate()->findOrFail', IssueTicket.php:42-48), and retries 5 times on a code collision. The write-once guard is an updating hook (Ticket.php:65-76). call() locks the row and checks state and membership (Ticket.php:120-147). The factories honour explicit codes and provide forQueue (TicketFactory.php:29-45). One gap: isCodeCollision only matches SQLSTATE '23000' (IssueTicket.php:74), so on PostgreSQL ('23505') the collision retry never runs.

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through the invokable app/Actions/IssueTicket. Fillable is set deliberately with the #[Fillable] attribute. Migrations have a reversible down(). CHANGELOG, business-rules.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md and docs/README.md are updated. PHPDoc is present on the public methods. One deviation: the conventions say authorization always goes through policies/gates, but Ticket::call() checks membership inline ('$user->membershipFor($entityId) === null', Ticket.php:135) with no policy or gate. The contract does put call() on the model.

security.evidence: call() enforces entity membership on the server, inside a transaction, after locking the ticket row (Ticket.php:127-137). Non-members leave the ticket unchanged, and tests cover this. Mass assignment is limited to fillable lists. Issuance re-reads queue state from the locked row, so a stale model cannot bypass a deactivation. No HTTP or Livewire surface is added. The only minor point is that the authorization check bypasses the policy layer, so it can't be reused or audited there.

tests.evidence: There are five Pest files under tests/Feature/Queue. They cover the default issuance fields; consecutive codes with custom priority and channel; negative priority and inactive queue rejected with nothing persisted; the stale-model deactivation case (IssueTicketTest.php:754-766); construction with no arguments; and a forced code-collision retry (IssueTicketTest.php:777-796). Code allocation is covered for legacy codes, insertion order with A999 then A1000, growth past 999, no reuse after delete, and per-queue scope. Call tests cover each role, a non-member, a member of another entity, a non-waiting ticket and a double call. Immutability is tested for every forbidden field, along with the allowed call-field updates. Schema, index and cascade tests are included.

simplicity.evidence: The code is direct, with no extra layers. Two things could be leaner. isCodeCollision parses SQLSTATE and the message by hand (IssueTicket.php:70-75) when Laravel already ships UniqueConstraintViolationException, which handles every driver. nextCode uses pluck('code') to load every code ever issued in the queue (Ticket.php:99-102) just to find the last valid one, so each issuance costs O(n). A lazy/cursor scan or a bounded query would avoid that. call() also checks the status twice, once outside the lock and once inside (Ticket.php:122 and 130), which is harmless.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (MUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUANCE, CODE_ATTEMPTS, isCodeCollision). Methods are small, and the comments explain the intent (Ticket.php:62-64, TicketFactory.php:32-33). The models and factories match Laravel's generated style. There is no dead code or debug output. One nit: the test helper is a long, prefixed global function (pegafilaQueueWaitingTicketForCallTest).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: migrations, models, enums, exception, action, factories, tests and the doc updates the task asks for. The architecture.md TODO about the single-call test is resolved in the same change. No HTTP, Livewire or call-next selection was added.

issues.explanation: isCodeCollision only accepts SQLSTATE '23000' (MySQL/SQLite), so on PostgreSQL ('23505') a concurrent unique collision is rethrown instead of retried. Catching Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException would handle every driver.
The membership check for calling is done inline in the model rather than through a policy or gate, but the conventions say authorization always goes through app/Policies.
nextCode uses pluck to load every code ever issued in the queue on each issuance, then stops at the first valid one, so the cost grows with queue history. A lazy or limited scan would avoid that.
The status check before the transaction duplicates the authoritative check made after the lock.
The global helper function pegafilaQueueWaitingTicketForCallTest has an awkward name; a Pest beforeEach or a dataset would be more idiomatic.

review.summary: The change implements the queue/ticket domain core: migrations, models, enums, the IssueTicket action with a locked re-read of the queue state and retry on code collision, the write-once guard, single-call authorization and the requested factories. Tests are thorough, covering every business-rule edge case, and the docs are kept in sync. I would approve with small fixes: the collision detection is MySQL/SQLite-specific, call authorization bypasses the policy layer, and nextCode loads every code in the queue on each issuance.
